entry.title: What is presented here is the #KareKheir report for Mordad 1405, and it reaches…
entry.summary:
Source: @yaser_arab57

What is presented here is the #KareKheir report for Mordad 1405, and it reaches you, dear ones, with the aim of letting you know how and where the funds you entrust to #KareKheir with various intentions have been spent. In the past month, the total amount spent in this regard was 240,562,397.5 Toman, which has grown by about 2 billion Toman compared to the previous month. Also, this month saw 3,063 recorded instances of assistance, which is about 350 more than the previous month. Furthermore, in Mordad, 9,732 deposits were made to the introduced accounts, which is about 600 more deposits than the previous month. In Mordad, the matter of school supplies was a priority, and we were able to secure and deposit half of the required budget for procuring these items; naturally, our priority in Shahrivar will be to secure the remaining half. Additionally, we owe about 500 million Toman for the reconstruction of 18 schools damaged by the war, which we must also settle in the coming month. The details of the actions and activities are presented in the attached charts, broken down accordingly. I am grateful to each and every one of you, dear ones, who have kept the light of this path burning. With respect.

entry.title: Vital ConversationsMohammad FazeliFor a society that has experienced the bloody…
entry.summary:
Source: @yaser_arab57

Vital ConversationsMohammad FazeliFor a society that has experienced the bloody and catastrophic events of #Aban_98 (November 2019), dialogue about any plan related to changing gasoline and energy policy is vital. For a society where the #energy_imbalance has reached a life-or-death threshold, dialogue about any plan related to changing gasoline and energy policy is vital. A conversation with economist Dr. #Mohsen_Yazdanpanah, published on the IranTalk media platform under the title "Gasoline Reforms: Without Fireworks," was an attempt to open the door to dialogue about a plan some in the government are pursuing, critique it, and highlight its consequences.Watching "Gasoline Reforms: Without Fireworks" — any plan can be critiqued, including the current government's plan; and any critique can also be critiqued, including those Mohsen Yazdanpanah levels against the current plan. What matters is that for any chronic and complex issue — such as energy in today's Iran — there is no better path than policy transparency, social dialogue, and building social and political consensus around the best solutions. All those interested in energy policy discussions and debates on price and non-price reforms in gasoline and other energy carriers can be invited to watch this conversation and engage in the social debate about it. These are vital conversations. @fazeli_mohammad

entry.title: 📌His bad state was obvious from the look of his shop. He's a religious man;…
entry.summary:
Source: @yaser_arab57

📌His bad state was obvious from the look of his shop. He's a religious man; I gave him my wife's novel to bind. He was pleasant-faced and well-spoken, at most 45 years old. He said: Can you pay now and make us happy? I said: Yes, why not. I generally have great respect for dying skilled trades like bookbinders. He swiped the card. Only 50,000 tomans! I was charmed by his fairness, politeness, and ethics. I said: Swipe another 50,000 tomans too! He said: Why? I said: A treat from me to you. He said: From morning till now I've earned 22,000 tomans. I bought two eggs, tomatoes, and bread, and it came to 70,000 tomans. Honestly, my heart sank. I said: The sky has darkened not just for you, but for a whole nation, unfortunately. Yes, to all of you whose lack today has nothing to do with yourselves and is the fruit of the ruling discrimination and injustice, at least forgive people like me for being a little—or perhaps only slightly—better off than you. You are experiencing a very difficult situation, much, much harder than the situation of people like me.... https://t.me/seyyedhashemfirouzi

entry.title: 📌The Incapable, the Ignorant, and the Culprits Environmental compulsion born…
entry.summary:
Source: @yaser_arab57

📌The Incapable, the Ignorant, and the Culprits Environmental compulsion born of inaction and misconduct builds prisons, and even a dove cannot bear a cage. It is for this reason that today, through my close friends, I learned that besides Sorena, another autistic child also threw himself from the height of his home, leaving the prison of the inactive and the malefactors to their fate. Inaction and misconduct have individual, collective, social, and structural roots. Inaction and misconduct on an individual level in this apocalyptic economic chaos are mostly born of helplessness and desperation, like the dear and captive parents of Sorena, whose wings were bound by the monster of imposed impoverishment, keeping them so busy that in the end, it took their fledgling dove from them. Saeed Roustaee, in his latest work "Woman & Child," opened a social-moral court in exploring the reasons for the free fall of the teenage boy, which is not unlike Sorena's story, at least in the structural dimension. Yes, truly, who were the ignorant, the incapable, and the culprits in the flight of Sorena, the teenager with autism? Which institutions and organizations, through structural misconduct and inaction, became the agents of this great pain for Sorena's family? Whose misconduct, in failing to prioritize and spending the public wealth of the captive nation on unnecessary paths, became the cause of Sorena's flight? How long is the social system, as a dynamic element unaware of the good, supposed to cook a pot of sholeh and give nazri (charitable food)... but remain indifferent to the real pains of the afflicted? From the Ministry of Education to the State Welfare Organization, from the Endowments Organization to all other institutions and the entire establishment, which have a prominent, active, and indeed irrelevant presence from Arbaeen to street gatherings and so on—each, according to the jurisprudential-legal rule of "Tasbib" (causation), what role did they play in the flight of the Sorena's of this land? Why is it that, fundamentally, dying in this soil is much easier and more accessible than the right to life? Why are the gates of death so easily open, while even the windows facing the courtyard and life are locked and chained for a bit of a better life? May God give patience to all the grieving mothers and fathers of this land, including Sorena's father and mother. And I hope that the glow of the sun once again brings the warmth of life back to this land. I also offer my condolences to my dear friend Yaser Arab, whose concern for solving the social issue of autism I have seen and observed up close. Dear Yaser, unfortunately, this is the land of unfulfilled wishes and efforts, even non-individual efforts for social well-being. https://t.me/seyyedhashemfirouzi

entry.title: Goodbye! I'm leaving for a while! Hopefully not forever... but for now, I'm…
entry.summary:
Source: @yaser_arab57

Goodbye! I'm leaving for a while! Hopefully not forever... but for now, I'm stepping away from social media for some time. Over these years, I've written about many things: children, Iran's development, official and unofficial media, the helplessness of autistic children, the sexual life of Iranians, social deafness, poverty alleviation, charity work, childhood and development, Baluchistan, the government, society, and many other things... I always thought that maybe if we talk about something correctly and precisely, if it gets seen, if a voice reaches somewhere, eventually something would happen... But these days, after hearing the cries of a mother who lost her child, I looked at myself and saw that I'm more tired than ever... Maybe I should be silent for a while and think. Think about where all this talking, writing, and analyzing actually helps, and where it just makes us think we're doing something? So for a while, I won't write, won't analyze, won't comment on anything... I think I need to go away for a while, think, and see if I really want to talk again afterward or not? The video is a clip from a documentary about Baluchistan that was produced years ago...@yaser_arab57
